title: Vertical battlecards and talk tracks
content:
Purpose: quick, tactical battlecards and customer-facing talk tracks for sales and solutions engineering when engaging Fintech, Healthcare, Legal, Enterprise SaaS, and Gov/Defense leads. This is a working doc — keep short lines, callouts, and friction points for quick copy/paste into calls or emails.

Status / how to use:
- Draft for SDRs, AEs, SEs to use as first-touch scripts and objection-handling notes.
- Not a final playbook — pull high-confidence claims into the official GTM playbook after validation (see TODOs).
- Owners: Samir (overall), Leah (healthcare), Miguel (gov/defense), Priya (fintech/legal).

Global positioning nugget (1 line):
- "Run LLMs with predictable latency, enterprise controls, and cost levers — from hosted API to fully private deployments."

Competitor shorthand (for quick reference):
- OpenAI / Anthropic: leader in model quality & API simplicity. Weakness: enterprise isolation + predictable SLOs at scale.
- Cohere / Hugging Face: model variety and fine-tuning. Weakness: end-to-end SLA, turnkey private deployments.
- Nvidia / OctoML / Triton users: strong infra but heavier ops burden for teams.
- Mosaic/Replicate: self-host friendly; tradeoff is operational work and fewer enterprise connectors.

Common cross-vertical objections and quick counters:
- "We already use OpenAI" -> "OpenAI for fast prototyping; Redwood lets you productionize with predictable latency, dedicated capacity, and enterprise isolation (VPC/KMS) while keeping model portability."
- "Sensitive data concerns" -> "Private control plane, audit logs, and KMS integrations; on-prem option for air-gapped regulatory needs."
- "Token cost is too high" -> "Optimize with intelligent batching, KV prefix caching, and quantized model variants — typical 2x-3x token-cost reductions for chat-heavy workloads."
- "We host ourselves" -> "If you want full control, Redwood Private gives a consistent control plane + ops accelerators vs rebuilding from scratch."

Vertical-specific notes and sample talk tracks
1) Fintech (payments, trading platforms, lending)
- Primary buyer personas: platform eng lead, head of risk/ML, product manager for automation, compliance officer.
- Key risks: data residency, auditability, explainability, latency for real-time risk checks.
- Value props that land: predictable latency for decisioning, cost-per-decision reductions, verifier-friendly audit logs.
- Example opening line (email): "We help teams move from prototype to 99% uptime inference for risk checks — lowering per-decision inference cost while keeping full audit trails and model versioning for compliance."
- Quick ROI example: a lending flow with 10k decisions/day at 150 tokens per decision. With hosted baseline cost $0.0004 per token -> $600/day. Applying batching & quantized model gives 2.4x reduction -> $250/day. Annualized ~ $130k savings. (adjust numbers during deal prep)
- Objections + counters: "We need explainability" -> show deterministic rollout + eval hooks; "Latency spikes" -> demo Dedicated pool + autoscale + canary fallback.
- Signals to accelerate to AE/SE: SOC2 + SOC2 Type II request, volumes >5k/day, latency <150ms requirement.

2) Healthcare (digital health, payer/provider automation)
- Personas: Chief Medical Information Officer, security/compliance lead, head of NLP/AI, integration lead.
- Must-haves: PHI handling, HIPAA BAAs, data residency, auditing, model evals for safety, human-in-loop gating for clinical decision support.
- Messaging focus: "Private deployments, BAAs, audit trails and verifiable rollout control for clinical safety and regulatory traceability."
- Talk track for a discovery call: "We can run inference in your VPC with HSM-backed keys, audit logs per request, and a private control plane so clinical data never leaves your approved boundary."
- Example case ask: number of docs/patient messages per day, retention window, required retention for compliance.
- Technical detail to prep: FIPS/KMS details, cert questions, and on-prem packaging timeline (typically multi-week planning).
- Red flags: ask what clinical group is signing off. If CTO pushes for instant deployment without SI/clinical review — slow down.

3) Legal (law firms, eDiscovery, contract review tools)
- Personas: Head of Legal Ops, Partner champion, InfoSec, Product lead for legal automation.
- Hot buttons: data confidentiality, model hallucination risk, reproducible outputs for audits.
- Core message: "Deterministic rollouts, model pinning, and retrievable request logs to support defensible outputs."
- Use-case script: document ingestion + semantic search + contract clause extraction. Emphasize embeddings and reranking for accuracy and combined validation UI.
- Compliance proof points to highlight: per-request audit log, retention policy controls, redact-at-ingest options.

4) Enterprise SaaS (B2B apps adding LLM features)
- Personas: product manager, platform engineering, CTO, growth lead.
- Drivers: time-to-market for LLM features, cost predictability, multi-tenant isolation, ability to A/B test model changes safely.
- Message: "Ship LLM features fast on hosted API, then move to Dedicated or Private as you hit SLOs or compliance needs. We support safe rollouts and per-route cost breakdowns so PMs can optimize feature economics."
- Useful opening: "Use hosted to prototype and measure real query patterns; when you need predictable throughput/latency, migrate to reserved pools with traffic shaping and automatic fallbacks."
- KPI examples to ask: token distribution, p95 latency requirement, concurrency targets, expected growth in queries/month.

5) Gov/Defense (federal agencies, defense contractors)
- Personas: Program manager, CISO, procurement lead, contracting officer.
- Critical constraints: FedRAMP? ITAR? Fed data residency, extreme audit requirements, supply chain assurances, air-gapped on-prem.
- Lead messaging: "Private control plane and on-prem packages built for high-assurance deployments, with auditability and optional HSM/KMS integration."
- Procurement note: long procurement cycles; start early with cert questions and provide a clear integration checklist for security teams.
- SE prep checklist: data flow diagrams, encryption-at-rest/in-transit specifics, attestation materials, and list of third-party components.

Detailed competitor play mapping (short):
- If customer cares about rapid prototyping + best-of-breed models -> mention OpenAI/Anthropic; pitch Redwood as the production path for the same workflows.
- If customer is building infra internally -> highlight total cost of ownership and operational velocity advantages of Redwood Private vs building orchestration + monitoring + kernel selection.
- If customer is cost-focused -> emphasize Redwood Optimize, batching + prefix caching examples, and model/quantization recommendations.

Notes to SEs on demos and POCs:
- Show a simple proof: 1) baseline hosted latency with sample prompt, 2) show dedicated pool performance and failover to smaller model, 3) demo cost analytics per-route, 4) show audit log and request replay.
- Keep POC scope small: 3 prompts, 1 embedding flow, 1 rerank flow. Track token counts before/after optimization.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate the 2.4x cost-reduction baseline with infra team across 3 common customer workloads (chat support, document QA, classification). Owner: infra (see JIRA:INF-680).
- Collect 3 anonymized healthcare BAAs and associated scripts for compliance playbook. Owner: Leah.
- Create a one-page FedRAMP/ITAR checklist for procurement cycles (Miguel).
- Build a short one-pager with concrete latency SLO examples and cost ranges per model size for AE handouts. Owner: product-marketing.

Quick snippets for outreach (copy/paste):
- Fintech subject line: "Cut per-decision inference cost while keeping audit trails for compliance"
- Healthcare opener: "HIPAA-ready inference in your VPC — full audit logs and HSM key control"
- Legal cold email: "Defensible contract review: model pinning, request logs, and rollback control"
- SaaS note: "Prototype on hosted API, migrate to Dedicated for predictable throughput — we help with the migration plan"
- Gov intro: "Private control plane + on-prem package for high-assurance deployments — integration checklist attached"

Historic references / links to copy into final playbook:
- Confluence draft: confluence:GT-verticals-playbook
- Relevant Jira tickets: JIRA:GT-3421 (verticals strategy), JIRA:INF-680 (cost validation).

Doc history / audit: created 2025-10-12 by Samir Patel. Major updates: 2026-02-20 added gov checklist items and ROI examples.

Remember: this is a working, shareable deck of short scripts and counters. Keep edits lean and add real customer numbers when available.
